title: Designing Systems That Actually Ship: A Small Template

cover.alt: A folded design document becomes a bounded modular structure with an input path and an inspection gate.

figures.title: Connect the plan to the repository
figures.summary: Four small pieces turn a general idea into a design another person can inspect.

items.label: Problem
items.detail: State what the system is intended to solve.

items.label: Inputs
items.detail: Identify what can enter the system and through which boundary.

items.label: Outputs
items.detail: Describe the result the system must produce.

items.label: File map
items.detail: Point each responsibility to an actual location in the codebase.

figures.caption: The document's core questions. The file map connects the written design to implementation.

figures.title: Make the design testable
figures.summary: Review the document before using it to drive implementation.

items.label: Artifact
items.detail: The design document exists and can be read.

items.label: Paths
items.detail: Every listed code path exists in the repository.

items.label: Boundaries
items.detail: Inside and outside responsibilities are explicit and do not overlap.

items.label: Data flow
items.detail: The described movement of data maps to real folders.

items.label: Completion
items.detail: Each done-when statement has a command, test or browser check.

figures.caption: These checks follow the article's verification questions; they do not establish that a project has passed them.
